provenance_note: Every reference value is recomputed by bench-src/ref/gen_cfd.py from the sources this artifact cites; that generator was re-run against this tree on 2026-10-03 and its output compared with the deployed corpus leaf by leaf at 405 leaves, 0 differing, so no case reuses a stored ref and none carries ref_source "recorded".
reference: Analytic well-mixed limits (dT = P/(rho cp Q), C = C_out + S/Q) and the exact conservation identities, derived and implemented independently in python, plus the de Vahl Davis (1983) Table I cavity - which is itself re-derived here from the governing equations by an independent stream-function/vorticity solver on 41/61/81 grids, because cfd.html carries the same published table at line 4583.  This is deliberately NOT a comparison against high-fidelity CFD: the tool is a reduced-order voxel solver and is graded on the laws that must hold at any fidelity.
reference_citations: G. de Vahl Davis, "Natural convection of air in a square cavity: a bench mark numerical solution", International Journal for Numerical Methods in Fluids 3 (1983) 249-264, Table I (Ra = 1e3 column; benchmark values are themselves a Richardson extrapolation of 41x41 / 61x61 / 81x81).

U. Ghia, K.N. Ghia, C.T. Shin, "High-Re solutions for incompressible flow using the Navier-Stokes equations and a multigrid method", Journal of Computational Physics 48 (1982) 387-411, Tables I and II (129x129 grid).  Carried, not executed.
ASHRAE Handbook - Fundamentals (2017), Chapter 1: dry air as an ideal gas, R_da = 287.042 J/(kg K), c_p of dry air 1006 J/(kg K) at room temperature.

E.W. Lemmon, R.T. Jacobsen, S.G. Penoncello, D.G. Friend, "Thermodynamic Properties of Air and Mixtures of Nitrogen, Argon, and Oxygen", J. Phys. Chem. Ref. Data 29 (2000) 331-385 - as implemented in CoolProp 8.0.0, used here for an independent rho*cp of the supply air.
ANSI/ASHRAE Standard 62.1, Table 6-2 (zone air-distribution effectiveness for mixing ventilation, 0.8-1.2) - the published band the volume-mean-versus-exhaust allowance is taken from.
tolerance: Conservation laws are graded tightly (1e-4 relative on the air balance, 2 % of gross turnover on the energy and tracer balances - the threshold the tool itself calls "good").  The well-mixed limits are graded with a 25 % allowance taken from ANSI/ASHRAE 62.1 Table 6-2 (air-distribution effectiveness 0.8-1.2), because the exhaust value is exact by balance while the VOLUME MEAN differs from it by the room's mixing quality.  The Boussinesq magnitude is graded at 15-25 % against de Vahl Davis on a coarse grid, a discretization window wide enough that only a genuinely wrong buoyancy coefficient fails.
environment: Chromium 141 (Playwright channel "chromium") started with --enable-unsafe-webgpu --enable-unsafe-swiftshader, running WebGPU on the SwiftShader software rasteriser (adapter reports google / swiftshader).  A stub for canvas.getContext("webgpu") replaces the swapchain with an offscreen texture, because with a real swapchain this driver loses the device during boot and again within seconds of Run - measured deviceLost 10 / recoveries 9 inside 5 s, ending in "WebGPU adapter is unavailable".  The compute path is untouched.  This is NOT the lavapipe software Vulkan driver the 2026-08-12 artifact records, and it is NOT the live GPU that REFACTOR_NOTES.md:34 requires before cfd can be merged.

stopping_rule.rule: every room scene is stopped on an EXACT STEP COUNT (CFD_STEPS, default 3000 = 1200 s of model time at the tool's default dt = 0.4 s, five nominal air changes at V/Q = 48/0.2 = 240 s and 1.7x the tool's own 720 s warm-up target), from a watcher inside the page that presses the tool's own Stop; the run then asserts it stopped on that step.  Not a wall-clock budget, and not the tool's steady-state detector.  Five air changes leaves exp(-5) = 0.67 % of the initial offset in a first-order fill, two orders inside the 25 % band the mean is graded in; the residual is not assumed, it is measured as the storage term of each ledger and reported.
stopping_rule.why: The superseded driver ran until sim.stat.done OR until a 900 s WALL-CLOCK budget expired, and did not fail on the timeout - it read whatever field happened to be there. Every mean it recorded is therefore a function of how fast the machine was.  This was not theoretical: an intermediate version of THIS driver polled the model time from node every 10 s, and two runs of the same scene stopped at steps 3009 and 3006, and at 3041 and 3006.  Three steps of a genuinely unsteady room moved the gross inflow through the relief opening by 13 % and the energy storage term by a factor of three.  Measured here, that matters: this room never satisfies the tool's own detector.  Its half-window T difference settles at 0.15-0.20 K against the 0.10 K tolerance and its velocity difference at 0.035-0.042 m/s against 0.02 m/s, and stays there past t = 1340 s - the buoyant plume over the 1 kW source is genuinely unsteady, which is a correct thing for a transient solver to report and not a defect.  A fixed model time makes the step count, and therefore every number below, identical on any machine.  The detector verdict and its half-window metrics are recorded next to each result under raw.run_state.
stopping_rule.residual_transient: How far from steady the stop actually is, is not asserted: it is the storage term of each ledger, reported in raw.energy.storage and raw.gas.storage against the gross turnover in the same block.

driver_surfaces.input: EDITOR.applyScene(VOXCFD.sceneFromJSON(scene)) - the declared-state entry point the runtime permalink and handoff use (cfd.html:7439); no DOM file input, no toast.
driver_surfaces.output: Diagram.record.build().outputs cross-checked against a direct sweep of EDITOR.sim.fields; agreement is itself a graded comparison in every MASS-BALANCE case.

not_benchmarked.lid_driven_cavity: The UI cannot express a lid-driven cavity: there is no moving-wall boundary condition anywhere in the room editor and no way to set a Reynolds number.  The solver core is reachable as window.VOXCFD.Fluid, but reaching steady state at Re = 100/400/1000 on a grid fine enough to compare with Ghia's 129x129 tables costs tens of hours on the software rasteriser available here, so no Ghia comparison is reported rather than one at a resolution that would say nothing.  The Ghia tables are carried in the reference file for a future run on real hardware.
not_benchmarked.high_Ra_cavity: de Vahl Davis at Ra = 1e5 and 1e6 needs a much finer grid and many more steps than the software rasteriser here allows; only the low-Ra case is reported, and it is the one that measures the buoyancy coefficient most directly.
not_benchmarked.gpu_gate: REFACTOR_NOTES.md:34 conditions merge on a run of the tool's internal gates on a LIVE GPU.  This box has no GPU.  Nothing in this file discharges that condition.
not_benchmarked.scene_identity: The scenes the 2026-08-12 artifact was measured on were never delivered (ref/cfd_ref.json is absent from this tree).  The scenes here are reconstructed from the inputs and raw blocks the artifact records; the graded laws are scene-robust, but the mixing-quality numbers (T_mean, C_mean) are not, so this run is NOT a like-for-like regression test against the artifact's recorded case values.

fidelity_benchmarks.note: Fidelity measurement, not a pass/fail: a 16x16 voxel grid cannot reproduce a benchmark extrapolated from 81x81.  The peak velocities are, however, a direct measure of the Boussinesq source g beta dT, so a large error here would mean a wrong buoyancy magnitude.

cases.note: Global air mass conservation: the sum of the inflows through every external boundary face must equal the sum of the outflows at steady state.  Read from the tool's own whole-room audit, cross-checked against the prescribed supply-fan flow.
cases.tolerance: |Qin - Qout| / Qin <= 1e-4 (a conservation law: it must hold to solver round-off, not to engineering accuracy); and the flow delivered through the supply-fan faces must be within 2 % of the prescribed fan flow.  The second test is deliberately read off the FAN faces alone: the passive relief opening exchanges air in both directions across its own face under buoyancy, so the gross inflow over all boundary faces is the fan flow PLUS that exchange.  That exchange is physical and grows as the mesh resolves the opening, so grading the gross inflow against the fan flow would penalise the finer mesh for being finer.  It is reported instead, under two_way_exchange_m3s, together with the ungraded gross-inflow comparison so that nothing is hidden by the choice.
cases.ref_source: recomputed - a conservation identity (sum of inflows = sum of outflows) plus the prescribed fan flow, which is an input

cases.note: Room energy balance at steady state: internal gains + envelope + advection must equal the rate of change of stored enthalpy, and the well-mixed limit dT = P/(rho cp Q) must be approached.  The envelope U is set to zero so the analytic limit is exact.
cases.tolerance: balance residual <= 2 % of the gross energy turnover (the threshold the tool itself calls "good"); mean room temperature rise within 25 % of the well-mixed rise - the exhaust value is exact by balance, the VOLUME MEAN differs from it by the room's mixing quality, for which ASHRAE 62.1 Table 6-2 gives 0.8-1.2 for mixing configurations, so 25 % is the published mixing band, not a physics tolerance; the measured effectiveness is reported alongside.  The well-mixed rise is evaluated with the tool's OWN declared rho*cp = 1.2*1005 J/(m3 K), because that is the constant its ledger has to close on; the 4 % by which that differs from dry air at the supply state is recorded as a crosscheck in the reference file, not buried in this tolerance.
cases.ref_source: recomputed - dT = P/(rho cp Q) derived and implemented in refsrc/make_cfd_ref.py, with the tool's own declared rho*cp; two independent property sets are carried as a crosscheck in the reference file

cases.note: Tracer mass balance: a steady source S with ventilation Q must give the analytic well-mixed concentration C = C_out + S/Q.
cases.tolerance: balance residual <= 2 % of the gross tracer turnover; mean concentration within 25 % of the well-mixed excess over ambient - the same published air-distribution-effectiveness band as for energy; the measured removal effectiveness is reported.  No fluid property enters this limit at all, so it is exact.
cases.ref_source: recomputed - C = C_out + S/Q, closed form, no fluid property enters it

cases.note: The same room solved on two meshes.  Conservation must hold on both (graded above) and the integral answers must agree: a well-mixed room temperature and concentration are set by the balances, not by the mesh, so they must be mesh-insensitive.
cases.tolerance: mean room temperature rise within 15 % between the two meshes and mean concentration excess within 30 %.  The integral balances pin the exhaust values exactly on every mesh (graded above); what changes with the mesh is only how well the room mixes.
cases.ref_source: recomputed - a mesh-to-mesh self-consistency requirement, no external reference value is involved

cases.note: A 2 kW source on the floor of a room whose only opening is high on the wall.  With the Boussinesq term of the right sign the warm air must rise: the ceiling layer must end up warmer than the floor layer and the net interior vertical velocity must be upward.  A sign error would give exactly the opposite, so this is a pass/fail test of the sign, not of the magnitude.
cases.tolerance: stratification dT (ceiling - floor) > 0.2 K and net interior vertical velocity > 0
cases.ref_source: recomputed - an inequality derived from the sign of the buoyancy term, not a number

cases.note: Magnitude of the Boussinesq source, measured through the de Vahl Davis cavity where the peak velocities scale directly with Ra = g beta dT L^3/(nu alpha).  This grades the buoyancy COEFFICIENT, not the fidelity of the flow field: a factor-of-two error in g beta would move u_max by ~40 % and Nu by ~20 %.  The reference is the published Table I, independently re-derived here (ref/cfd_ref.json, fidelity.DVD_rederived) because cfd.html carries the same table at line 4583 and quoting it alone would not be independent of the tool.
cases.tolerance: u_max and w_max within 25 % and Nu within 15 % of the de Vahl Davis benchmark on this coarse grid.  The window is the discretization error of an N=16 grid against an 81x81 extrapolation, not a physics tolerance; it is wide enough that only a genuinely wrong buoyancy coefficient fails it.

distinct_results_detail.comment: Nine graded cases come from FOUR driven scenes by construction, and that is the shipped artifact's own design, not a selector failure: the mass, energy and tracer cases each read a different ledger out of the SAME solve of one room, GRID-CONVERGENCE is derived from the two room solves, and the cavity is its own scene.  Both counts are therefore reported.  Four scenes produced four distinct fingerprints (grid, step, T_mean, C_mean, qIn, fan inflow) and nine cases produced nine distinct comparison payloads, so no case is a frozen duplicate of another.

h0.25.note: Derived after the run from the raw values recorded above; not a new measurement.

ventilation.comment: The relief opening in the reconstructed scene is FREE (zeta = 0) and sits low on the wall, so buoyancy drives a large two-way exchange across it: 24 % of the fan flow on the 0.25 m mesh and 37 % on the 0.5 m mesh, against the 2.7 % / <0.1 % the 2026-08-12 artifact records.  That is a property of the reconstructed opening, not of the tool, and it is why MASS-BALANCE is graded on the FAN faces (as the shipped artifact's own tolerance paragraph says it must be) and not on the gross inflow.  Graded on the gross inflow at the same 2 % limit - which is what the superseded driver in /root/bench-src/run_cfd.mjs actually did - this scene would read 24 % and 37 % and FAIL.  Recorded here so the choice of key is visible rather than buried.

well_mixed_limits.comment: Two well-mixed limits exist for this room and they differ, because the relief opening breathes: one on the prescribed FAN flow (the quantity the case is graded against, and the one the artifact used) and one on the measured TOTAL boundary outflow.  Both are reported.  The measured volume mean sits between them, above the total-outflow limit because a low exhaust removes relatively cool floor air - the resulting air-distribution effectiveness is inside the 0.8-1.2 band ANSI/ASHRAE 62.1 Table 6-2 gives for mixing ventilation, which is the band the 25 % allowance was taken from.

residual_transient.comment: The ledger CLOSES (residual 4e-4 to 8e-4 of gross turnover) but the field is not motionless: the instantaneous storage term at the stop is 6-7 % of the 1000 W input, and the tool's own steady-state detector never fires on either mesh.  One snapshot pair cannot separate a secular drift from turbulent fluctuation, and this run does not claim to: what it claims is that the volume mean is within 2.7 % (0.25 m) and 5.0 % (0.5 m) of the analytic well-mixed limit, and that the two meshes - independent solves - agree with each other to 2.5 % on dT and 8.3 % on dC.  It does NOT claim the room reached steady state.

buoyancy_sign.note: Derived after the run from the raw values recorded above; not a new measurement.
buoyancy_sign.comment: The stratification half of this case is the half that carries the sign: +0.50 K from floor layer to ceiling layer.  The `mean_updraft` half is weaker than it looks and is recorded here so nobody reads more into it than it says.  In a room whose only opening is at z = 3.0-4.0 m, the horizontal-plane average of w must be zero at every level BELOW the opening by mass conservation, whatever the plume is doing - and it measures 1e-8 m/s there, which is a statement about the solver's mass conservation, not about buoyancy.  The 6.8e-3 m/s in the top two layers is the net outflow through the opening.  So `mean_updraft > 0` tests the flux across the opening; it does not test the plume.
